sounds.intro: Dutch is written in the Latin alphabet. It sounds a lot like a mix of English and German. Nouns are "de" or "het" words, and you must learn which for each noun. The stress is usually on the first syllable.
rows: a scratchy sound at the back of the throat, like "ch" in Scottish "loch"
a sound like "ow" in "house", with rounded lips
like "ay" in "day" but a bit sharper
notes: Long vowels are written double in a closed syllable (aa, ee, oo, uu), and single in an open syllable (maken, not maaken).

grammar.title: Pronouns
text: Dutch always uses the pronoun. "Je" is informal and "u" is formal. "Hij" is he, "zij" or "ze" is she, "het" is it.

grammar.title: Singular and plural
text: Most nouns add -en or -s: boek, boeken. Some change a letter: huis, huizen. After a number the plural is used: twee boeken.

grammar.title: To be: zijn
text: "Zijn" (to be) is irregular. Learn all the forms.

grammar.title: Hebben: have
text: "Hebben" (to have): ik heb, jij hebt, hij heeft, wij hebben. "Er is" means "there is".

grammar.title: Present tense
text: Take the stem (werken, werk-) and add: -, -t, -t, -en. Werken (to work): ik werk, jij werkt, hij werkt, wij werken.

grammar.title: Basic sentences
text: The verb is always the second item: Ik lees een boek. If another word comes first, the verb still stays second: Vandaag lees ik een boek.

grammar.title: Negation
text: Use "niet" for verbs and adjectives, and "geen" for nouns with "een": Ik heb geen auto.
ex: I do not have a car
he does not work on Sundays

grammar.title: Asking questions
text: Put the verb first: Ben je student? A question word goes before the verb: Waar woon je?

grammar.title: Question words
text: A question word comes first, then the verb.

grammar.title: Possessives and liking
text: Put the word before the noun: mijn (my), jouw / je (your), zijn (his), haar (her), ons or onze (our), uw (your, formal), hun (their). To like something, use "leuk vinden" or "houden van".

grammar.title: Formal vs informal
text: jij / je (informal): friends, family, children. u (formal): strangers, older people, work. The verb changes only a little: je hebt, u hebt.
rows: hoe gaat het met je? / met u?
hoo khaht uht met yuh / met oo

grammar.title: Past and future (simple)
text: Past: the perfect tense, "hebben" or "zijn" + ge-...-d / -t. Ik heb gewerkt (I worked). Future: "gaan" + verb, or just the present with a time word.
ex: wij zijn naar het park gegaan
vay zayn nahr uht park khuh-KHAHN

grammar.title: Commands
text: Informal: the verb stem (kom). Formal: stem + t, with "u" (komt u). To forbid, use "niet" or "geen".

grammar.title: Can, must, want
text: Kunnen (can): ik kan. Moeten (must): ik moet. Willen (want): ik wil. The second verb goes to the end, in its basic form.
ex: I do not want to eat

grammar.title: In, on, at
text: Common words: in (in), op (on), bij (at, near), naar (to), van (from, of), met (with), onder (under).
ex: the book is on the table
het boek ligt op de tafel
uht book likht op duh TAH-fuhl
the cat is under the table
de kat zit onder de tafel
duh kat zit ON-duhr duh TAH-fuhl
the shop is next to the bank
de winkel is naast de bank
duh VING-kuhl is nahst duh bank
the park is near the station
het park is bij het station
uht park is bay uht stah-SHON
de les is om negen uur
duh les is om NAY-khuhn oor
the key is in the bag
de sleutel zit in de tas
duh SLUH-tuhl zit in duh tas

grammar.title: Comparing things
text: Add -er for "more": groot, groter. For "the most" add -st: groot, grootst (het grootste). "Than" is "dan". Irregular: goed, beter, best.
